title: Number of Islands
statement: Given an m x n grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands. An island is a group of connected '1's using only up, down, left and right connections.

examples.explanation: There are two small islands in the top left and one in the bottom left.

hints.content: What you are counting is the number of connected components. Which traversal finds components?
Every time you find land that has not been visited, you have found a new island. Then you must mark everything reachable from it.
DFS with recursion, or BFS with a queue. Either way you mark cells visited as soon as you add them to the traversal.
Changing visited land to '0' in place avoids a separate visited array, but be careful because it modifies the input grid.

pseudocode: floodFill from this cell, turning every reachable land into water
invariant: After each flood fill, every cell belonging to the island just counted is marked, so no island can be counted twice.
whyThisPattern: The question is a component count, and DFS or BFS is the standard way to explore a component. Marking on insert rather than on removal guarantees each cell is visited once, which keeps the whole grid linear.
bruteForce: Comparing each land cell against every other land cell to decide if they are connected is O((m * n)^2) in the worst case and can also miss connectivity through long chains. A single traversal touches each cell at most four times.
interviewExplanation: I scan the grid and every time I find an unvisited land cell I count a new island and flood fill from it, marking all reachable land as visited. Using a stack for the flood fill avoids deep recursion on a large grid, and marking a cell visited when it is pushed means it is never processed twice. This gives O(m * n) time.
commonMistakes: Marking cells visited when they are popped instead of when they are pushed, which causes repeated work.
Using diagonal neighbours, which counts diagonally touching land as one island.
Forgetting to count the island before starting the flood fill.

animationSteps.description: Land at row 0, column 0 starts a new island.

animationSteps.title: Flood fill the component
animationSteps.description: The traversal marks all three connected land cells.
animationSteps.text: Flood fill from row 0 column 0 visits row 0 column 1 and row 1 column 1, so that island contains three cells.

animationSteps.description: Back at the scan position: is the bottom left cell a new island?
animationSteps.text: Cell row 2 column 0 is land and is not connected to the first island. Choose what happens next.

payload.prompt: Row 2, column 0 is land with no visited neighbours. What happens?
payload.explanation: Unvisited land that is not connected to a counted island always starts a new island.

animationSteps.title: Three islands total
animationSteps.description: Two small islands and one single cell island.
animationSteps.text: The scan finds three islands: the two cell island in the top left, the single cell island below it and the single cell island at row 2 column 0.

animationSteps.description: Each land cell was visited exactly once.
animationSteps.text: The answer is 3 islands and every land cell was visited exactly once during the traversal.
